t: Minimum Moves to Pick K Ones — Sliding Window over Ones
o: Alice stands somewhere, instantly takes a one under her feet, then either spends 1 move to conjure a one at any zero cell (limited by maxChanges) or spends 1 move per step sliding an adjacent one toward herself. Conjured ones cost exactly 2 moves each (create next to Alice, then one swap into her). Real ones cost their distance to Alice. So with c = min(maxChanges, k) conjured ones, Alice walks to collect the k − c nearest real ones around her position; her move count is Σ|posᵢ − p| + 2c. Example 1: stand at index 1, take the local one, then 1 creation + 2 swaps = 3 moves. Example 2 has no ones at all, so 2 creations × 2 moves = 4.
k: A created one always costs exactly 2 moves (create adjacent + swap), independent of position.
Real ones are worth walking to only when cheaper than 2 moves, so the walked set is a contiguous window of the sorted one-positions around the median.
It suffices to examine windows of size need = k − c and need + 1: enlarging further adds more walking distance than the 2 moves saved.

a.i: Collect positions of existing ones and prefix sums. For a window of consecutive ones [i, j], the best standing point is a weighted median, and the total walking cost Σ|posₜ − p| splits into left/right halves computable in O(1) via prefix sums. Slide windows of size need and need+1, add 2·(k − windowSize) for the conjured ones, and take the minimum. When need = 0, the baseline is simply 2k (improved by size-1 windows where Alice stands on a real one for free).
s: Build pos (indices of ones) and its prefix sums.
Set c = min(maxChanges, k), need = k − c; if need = 0 initialize ans = 2k.
For window sizes need and need+1, slide over pos: cost = median absolute-deviation sum via prefix sums + 2(k − size).
a.t: O(n) — collecting positions and sliding constant-time windows over them.
a.sp: O(n) — position list and prefix sums.

w: Reason carefully about why 2 moves per created one is a hard floor and why windows larger than need+1 never help (marginal walking distance exceeds the 2-move saving). Pitfalls: forgetting the free pickup at the start (handled by the median cost including the standing cell), overflow of coordinate sums (use 64-bit), and the need = 0 corner. Follow-ups: return Alice's optimal starting index, or handle maxChanges = 0 (pure median window of size k).
